title: A 44 m fire column made of cotton and cellophane, cast by a hero who's 1.75 m tall (early prototype)
author: joaocamu
selftext:
The spell is built like an effect on a model railway, with tufts of cotton and flat strips of cellophane, lit from the inside. It's a column of fire 25 times taller than the wizard who casts it. In the video it lands on a crowd of about 1,500 undead walking through a street.

Right now the game is a city block made of voxels (everything will be destructible), filmed like a tilt-shift time-lapse. The camera stays high, the focus band is narrow, the sun is hard, and the cars, shadows and clouds run fast.

The game is meant to be an outbreak that starts small and silly, and grows until the end of the world. An action RPG against undead hordes, with loot and a skill tree. One hero, an archmage where every spell is far bigger than he is. 

It's very early. So far there's only a technical proof: the block, the camera, the light, the horde (up to 4,000 at 60 fps on my setup) and this one spell. There's no gameplay, combat or loot yet. I'm designing those next before coding with Claude, which should take a couple of weeks.

Built in Godot 4 with C++. Feedback on how it reads is very welcome, especially the scale and the miniature look.
